messages.author: 3deb10e6d08d6696
messages.subject: Problem with running time
parts:
Hi everyone,
I'm having trouble with my dataset. I think it will take weeks to run. It consist of 1065 capture event, divided int 7 primary and 18 secondary occasions. Additionally I have also D and g0 covariates. I tried to run a null model but after a whole day it aborted and said memory full. I tried collapsing all the secondary occasions into one primary but nothing changed. I tried with ncores=4 but it didn't seem to run better (after 37 minutes didn't ended one run of the null model).

Any other advice, altough I think I have to run separately every session...

I have a PC, 64 bit, intel I5 quadcore 2.5 GHz, 4 GB RAM.

Regards
Marco Basile

messages.author: a962fffd7a5358b2
messages.subject: Re: Problem with running time
parts:
Hi Marco,
A couple of suggestions that might help:
The number of points in your habitat mask/integration mesh has a big effect on computation time. Check that the extent and resolution of the mask aren't more than is required.
You can also try using memory.size() or memory.limit() to increase the amount of RAM R uses. 
Eric

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Problem with running time
parts:
Collapsing occasions is certainly a good idea, and I'd advise you to persist with that. Using multiple cores never seems to help much in secr.fit() because of the overheads in handling the worker processes. Not sure what you mean by one mesh per trap, so mask size could still be a problem (I would aim for nrow(mask) 1000-2000. Try running sessions separately. 4Gb is not an awful lot, but I survived with that until upgrading last week.
Murray

Hello Marco
I don't really think you have too much data, and I'm still hoping this is solvable by carefully configuring the analysis. ~t models are usually a waste of time (slow to fit because of the extra parameters, and negligible change in density estimates). I don't quite understand your layout - 130 polygons? If you are still stuck you could send me the data for one session offline and I'll take it as a challenge.
Murray
